top_violation_types.title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A report was not made to Child Care Regulation for an incident that potentially posed a risk to children.

top_violation_types.title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §747.605(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One out of four children's files evaluated lacked an address for the emergency contact.

top_violation_types.title: Written Operational Policies - Animals (26 TAC §747.501(7))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operational policies are missing information on animals present at the home.

top_violation_types.title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One out of four employees was pending 10 hours of annual training hours.    One out of four employees was pending 6 hours in business.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Relate to Children (26 TAC §746.1201(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Evidence obtained during the investigation shows that a staff member was not relating to children with courtesy or respect as they called children names that were not kind.

top_violation_types.title: Discipline - Teaches Acceptable Behavior and Self-control (26 TAC §746.2803(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on the information obtained, it was determined the operations discipline methods does not teach acceptable behavior and self-control.

top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the course of an investigation, it was determined that a caregiver was yelling at children.

top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on information obtained I observed a caregiver pulling a child to the ground and holding in a restraint hold.
